record.original_question: Does there exist a connected signed graph Γ = (G, σ) whose underlying graph G is not complete, whose adjacency spectrum is symmetric with respect to the origin, but which is not sign-symmetric, meaning Γ is not switching isomorphic to its negation -Γ = (G, -σ)?

evidence.quote: A signed graph Γ = (G, σ) is said to be sign-symmetric if Γ is switching isomorphic to its negation, that is, −Γ = (G, −σ).
Problem 3.3. Are there non-complete connected signed graphs whose spectrum is symmetric with respect to the origin but they are not sign-symmetric?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $\Gamma=(G,\sigma)$, where $G=(V,E)$ is a simple graph and $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$ is a sign function on its edges. The adjacency matrix $A(\Gamma)$ is the $|V|\times|V|$ matrix whose $(u,v)$-entry equals $\sigma(uv)$ if $uv\in E$ and $0$ otherwise; the spectrum of $\Gamma$ is the multiset of eigenvalues of $A(\Gamma)$. The negation of $\Gamma$ is $-\Gamma=(G,-\sigma)$. A switching at a vertex set $U\subseteq V$ replaces $\sigma(uv)$ by $-\sigma(uv)$ for every edge $uv$ with exactly one endpoint in $U$; two signed graphs on the same underlying graph are switching isomorphic if one can be obtained from the other by a vertex permutation followed by a switching. The signed graph $\Gamma$ is called sign-symmetric if $\Gamma$ is switching isomorphic to $-\Gamma$. (Sign-symmetry implies that the spectrum of $\Gamma$ is symmetric with respect to the origin.)

Question: Does there exist a connected signed graph $\Gamma=(G,\sigma)$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $G$ is not a complete graph,
\item the spectrum of $\Gamma$ is symmetric with respect to the origin, and
\item $\Gamma$ is not sign-symmetric (equivalently, $\Gamma$ is not switching isomorphic to $-\Gamma$)?
\end{enumerate}
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been answered affirmatively. Ghorbani, Majidi and others (e.g., "Connected non-complete signed graphs which have symmetric spectrum but are not sign-symmetric", Examples and Counterexamples, 2021) constructed explicit connected non-complete signed graphs whose spectrum is symmetric about zero but which are not sign-symmetric. Subsequent work (Li–Huang, arXiv:2304.06864) provides further infinite families via Cartesian and corona products.

status_evidence.title: Connected non-complete signed graphs which have symmetric spectrum but are not sign-symmetric
status_evidence.snippet: Examples and Counterexamples paper explicitly constructing such signed graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of connected non-complete signed graphs with symmetric spectrum that are not sign-symmetric is established.

status_evidence.title: Signed graphs with symmetric spectra
status_evidence.snippet: Provides infinite families of SSNSS (symmetric-spectrum non-sign-symmetric) signed graphs via Cartesian and corona products.
status_evidence.claim: Further constructions of such signed graphs exist, confirming the affirmative answer.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in the spectral theory of signed graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing the problem on sign-symmetry vs symmetric spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the problem and its resolution context.
